title: Kony 2012
analysis: This is Adichie's single story at viral scale. Northern Uganda is shown through one villain and helpless victims, with an American as the hero. It matches her picture of Africans waiting to be saved by a kind, white foreigner.

title: My response to Invisible Children's campaign
analysis: A Ugandan journalist takes back the power to tell the story. Adichie says power is not just telling someone's story but making it the definitive one. Kagumire refuses to let Kony 2012 be that story and centers Ugandan recovery and agency.
limits: Her group said it preferred a few viewers who wanted the truth over millions consuming a simple story. The counter-narrative existed but did not get the same reach as the original.

title: Security fears as Obama heads to terror hotbed
analysis: Nyabola argues CNN treated violence in Kenya as the norm instead of the exception. She says reports like this assume Kenyans will not see them, will not react, or can be ignored.

title: #SomeoneTellCNN
analysis: Nyabola uses this hashtag as her main example of a networked public sphere, where Kenyans online build a locally driven counternarrative and push international media toward more balanced coverage.
limits: CNN only changed Kenya to East Africa, so the frame mostly stayed. Nyabola also notes Kenyans online are a subset of a subset: people with electricity, internet access, and social media accounts.

title: The Hopeless Continent cover
analysis: The cover treats a whole continent as one place and blames its problems on culture. Ranger shows colonial officials did something similar, freezing flexible African custom into fixed tradition and inventing tribes to rule through. Adichie calls this showing a people as one thing over and over.

title: #TheAfricaTheMediaNeverShowsYou
analysis: This is what Adichie, quoting Achebe, calls a balance of stories. People posted cities, weddings, and campuses to show many Africas instead of one.
limits: It spread partly because Western outlets like NPR and HuffPost covered it, so Western media still shaped what got amplified. Swapping bad images for only good ones can risk becoming its own single story.
